## 2. Rewritten page

# HVAC scheduling and dispatch software built for small contractors

Fieldnote is HVAC scheduling and dispatch software used by 1,200 HVAC companies. The median customer runs six technicians, so half of Fieldnote's customers have six techs or fewer. Dispatchers plan the day on a drag-and-drop board, technicians work from a mobile app that keeps running without signal, and customers, invoices and payments sync both ways with QuickBooks Online. Plans start at $39 per user per month. Start a 14-day free trial — no credit card required.

## Schedule and dispatch from one board

The dispatch board shows every technician's day side by side. Drag a job to a new time slot or a different technician to reschedule it. Turn on automatic assignment and Fieldnote picks the technician based on the skills the job needs and how far each tech is from the site. Recurring maintenance agreements go on the schedule automatically, so spring and fall tune-ups don't have to be re-entered each season.

## Two-way sync with QuickBooks Online

Fieldnote syncs customers, invoices and payments in both directions with QuickBooks Online. An invoice created in Fieldnote appears in QuickBooks Online; a customer record edited in QuickBooks Online updates in Fieldnote. Fieldnote does not support QuickBooks Desktop — we'd rather tell you here than after you've started a trial.

## The technician app works offline

Mechanical rooms and basements don't have signal. The Fieldnote technician mobile app works offline and syncs its changes when the phone is back online. The office web app that dispatchers use does need an internet connection. If you've read elsewhere that "Fieldnote requires an internet connection," that is true only of the office app.

## Built for small HVAC companies

Fieldnote is used by 1,200 HVAC companies; the median customer has six technicians. In a March 2025 survey of 210 customers, dispatchers reported cutting the time they spend scheduling from 9 hours a week to 4. That figure is self-reported, so treat it as what customers told us, not a guarantee.

## Pricing

Fieldnote costs $39 per user per month billed annually, or $49 per user per month month-to-month. There is no free plan. Every account starts with a 14-day free trial; no credit card is taken, so the trial can't roll into a paid plan unless you choose one.

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does Fieldnote cost?**
Fieldnote costs $39 per user per month billed annually, or $49 per user per month on a month-to-month plan. There is no free plan. New accounts start with a 14-day free trial, and no credit card is required.

**Is there a free version of Fieldnote?**
No. Fieldnote has no free plan. It offers a 14-day free trial with no credit card required; after that, plans cost $39 per user per month billed annually or $49 per user per month month-to-month.

**Does Fieldnote work offline?**
Partly. The Fieldnote technician mobile app works offline and syncs its changes when the device is back online. The Fieldnote office web app, which dispatchers use, requires an internet connection.

**Does Fieldnote integrate with QuickBooks?**
Fieldnote integrates with QuickBooks Online through a two-way sync of customers, invoices and payments. Fieldnote does not support QuickBooks Desktop.

**How does Fieldnote assign jobs to technicians?**
Dispatchers can drag and drop jobs on Fieldnote's dispatch board, or turn on automatic assignment, which chooses a technician based on the skills the job requires and each technician's distance from the job site. Visits under recurring maintenance agreements are added to the schedule automatically.

**Is Fieldnote a good fit for a small HVAC company?**
Fieldnote is used by 1,200 HVAC companies, and the median customer has six technicians. In a March 2025 survey of 210 Fieldnote customers, dispatchers reported cutting their weekly scheduling time from 9 hours to 4.

## 4. Blog post and internal linking plan

- **Re-scope `/blog/hvac-scheduling-guide` to pure how-to intent.** Retitle it along the lines of "How to Schedule HVAC Jobs: A Dispatcher's Guide" and remove the exact phrase "HVAC scheduling software" from its title tag and H1, so the two URLs stop swapping for the head term.
- **Add one callout in the guide** linking here with the anchor "HVAC scheduling software," and link its offline and QuickBooks mentions to this page's FAQ anchors (`#faq-offline`, `#faq-quickbooks`) so crawlers and answer engines find the corrected statements.
- **Link back from this page's "Built for small HVAC companies" section** to the guide, so the pair reads as one topic cluster with two distinct intents.
- **Audit nav, footer, help center and pricing page:** every internal link with a "scheduling software" or "dispatch software" anchor should point here, not to the blog.
- **Re-check Search Console in 4–6 weeks.** If the URLs still alternate, fold any remaining commercial content from the guide into this page and keep the guide strictly how-to.

## 5. Rationale

Targeted "hvac scheduling software" (18,400 impressions, already page one) and "hvac dispatch software" (same product, same intent): both now appear in the title, H1 and dedicated H2s, and the blog cannibalization is being resolved. Also targeted the two accuracy queries: "does fieldnote work offline" and "hvac software quickbooks integration". The current AI answer on offline is wrong, and the old "Works with QuickBooks" line hid the Desktop gap; short, quotable statements fix both. "fieldnote pricing" just needed correct numbers — the page said $29, which is false.

Deliberately not targeted: "hvac scheduling app free", because there is no free plan, so ranking for it buys bounces and misleads; one honest FAQ answers it instead. "best hvac software for small business" is listicle intent a product page won't win; we cover the small-business angle with real numbers (median six technicians) and leave the head term to a future comparison post.
